clue.text: Playing a lush wartime song

indicators.note: playing something means performing or toying with it, so the letters are set to a fresh tune and order

blocks.note: the twelve letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A band strikes up a romantic, drunken number from the war years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A lush wartime song' reads like a description of a tune; 'lush' and 'wartime' are only letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: The Beatles recorded this track in 1967, so it is a specific example of a pop number.

clue.text: Annoyed, somewhat shirk education

indicators.note: somewhat means only to a degree, so only part of the following words is used

blocks.note: found running across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: Someone is annoyed because a student has been dodging school.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit inside shIRK EDucation.
explanation.definitionFit: To irk someone is to bother or vex them, so both words describe a person who has been irritated.

clue.text: A greater number turned up, touring British seaside town

indicators.note: to tour a place is to travel all round it, so one piece goes around another

blocks.note: more means a greater number
to turn up is to arrive, past tense
B is the abbreviation for British

explanation.surface: Bigger crowds than expected arrived on a tour of a British resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned up' looks like a reversal signal in a down clue, but it simply means arrived. CAME goes round B. Morecambe is a resort on the Lancashire coast of north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Morecambe lies on the bay of the same name and is a traditional holiday resort by the coast.

clue.text: Well, that man on vacation hastily grabs key

indicators.note: a vacated building is emptied, so the word loses its interior and keeps only its ends
grabbing something means closing a hand round it, so one piece is held inside another

blocks.note: the pronoun for a man already mentioned
only the first and last letters of the word
ALT is a key on a computer keyboard

explanation.surface: A man leaving for his holidays snatches up a key in a rush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well' opens the clue like an interjection, but it is the definition. The key is the one on a computer keyboard, and both pieces before it together do the grabbing.
explanation.definitionFit: Being well means being in good health, so the adjective for fit and not ill is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Stop working with listener from France

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for with
the ear is the organ that listens
of can mean from, as in a man of Kent
F is the international code for France

explanation.surface: Someone downs tools alongside a French eavesdropper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From France' reads as one phrase about nationality, but it splits into two pieces, OF and the country code F.
explanation.definitionFit: When a drug or effect wears off it gradually ceases to act, so the phrasal verb matches ceasing to function.

clue.text: King in play – that’s obvious, but not initially

indicators.note: not initially means without the start, so the opening letter is dropped

blocks.note: clear means obvious

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that the royal figure in a drama is plain to see.
explanation.walkthrough: CLEAR loses its C. The definition is the whole phrase: Shakespeare's tragic monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare wrote a tragedy about an elderly British monarch who divides his realm among his daughters.

clue.text: Found out a Parisian company sits on extremely valuable wine

indicators.note: extremes are the far ends of something, so only the first and last letters are kept

blocks.note: the French for a
CO is the abbreviation for company
the first and last letters of the word
red is a kind of wine

explanation.surface: A French firm is discovered sitting on a stock of very costly vintages.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'sits on' puts the first pieces above the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To uncover a secret is to discover or expose it, so both describe something revealed.

clue.text: Primates in church, troublemakers

blocks.note: CH is the abbreviation for church
imps are mischievous little devils

explanation.surface: Apes causing havoc during a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' suggests a container, but it only links the definition to the wordplay; the pieces are simply joined.
explanation.definitionFit: Chimpanzees are great apes, and apes belong to the order of mammals that includes monkeys and humans.

clue.text: Founder of genetics and soldiers from the south were in front

indicators.note: in a down entry, reading from the bottom up means the letters run backwards

blocks.note: ordinary soldiers are men
to lead is to be in front, past tense

explanation.surface: A pioneering scientist and troops advancing from the south led the way.
explanation.walkthrough: Only LED is read upwards; MEN stays as it is.
explanation.definitionFit: Gregor Mendel, an Austrian monk, worked out the laws of inheritance by breeding pea plants.

clue.text: Walker regularly thrives by river, covering kilometres

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken
to cover something is to go over and around it, so one piece wraps another

blocks.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters
K is short for kilometres
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A rambler flourishes beside a river, clocking up the kilometres.
explanation.walkthrough: HIE and R sit side by side, and together they wrap K.
explanation.definitionFit: A hiker is someone who goes on long walks in the countryside, so the terms are synonyms.

clue.text: Canal he repaired after a very heavy fall

indicators.note: something repaired has been taken apart and rebuilt, so the letters are reworked

blocks.note: taken as written
V is the abbreviation for very
the letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A man fixed a waterway following a serious tumble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heavy fall' reads like an accident, but it is the definition; 'after' places A and V in front of the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An avalanche is a huge mass of snow and ice sliding down a mountainside.

clue.text: Negotiation to purchase cold tablets, perhaps

indicators.note: a purchase is also a grip or hold, so one piece is gripped inside another

blocks.note: mediation is negotiating between parties
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: Bargaining over buying some cold remedies from the chemist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Purchase' looks like buying, but here it means a firm grip. 'Perhaps' warns that tablets are only one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Pills are one form of medicine taken to treat an illness, hence an example of the broader term.

clue.text: Characters in studio videoing poet

indicators.note: characters are letters, and these letters sit inside the words that follow

blocks.note: straddling the two words

explanation.surface: Some people are filming a writer in a studio.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across studiO VIDeoing.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovid was a Roman writer of verse, best known for the Metamorphoses.

clue.text: Delicious part of rugby game, gosh!

blocks.note: the scrum is the set piece where forwards bind and push against each other
my! is an exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: A rugby fan exclaims at how tasty the match-day food is.
explanation.walkthrough: Scrummy is informal British slang for tasty.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrummy is a playful British word for food that tastes wonderful, a blend of scrumptious and yummy.

clue.text: Feels bitter about ID for long-term inhabitants

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece surrounds another

blocks.note: to resent is to feel bitter about
taken as written

explanation.surface: Locals are sore about having to carry identity cards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Feels bitter about' reads as one phrase, but 'about' is the container signal and RESENTS alone is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Residents are people who live permanently in a place, rather than visitors passing through.

clue.text: With power divided, occasionally feel Los Angeles communist must make a comeback

indicators.note: occasionally means now and then, so only every other letter is used
to come back is to return the way you came, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: the first and third letters, taken alternately
LA is the abbreviation for Los Angeles
red is a familiar term for a communist

explanation.surface: A political pundit suggests a Californian leftist should return to public life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With power divided' looks like wordplay but is the definition; only the city and the communist are turned around, not the opening letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A federal system splits authority between a central government and regional states or provinces.

clue.text: Give two lines on old sculptor

blocks.note: to donate is to give
L stands for line, doubled
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: An instruction to write a couple of lines about a long-dead artist.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts LL above O.
explanation.definitionFit: Donatello was an Italian Renaissance artist famous for his bronze David and marble statues.

clue.text: Closely examine e.g. beetle seen around piano

indicators.note: something seen around another thing encircles it, so one piece holds another

blocks.note: a beetle is an example of an insect
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly

explanation.surface: Someone peers at a beetle crawling round a piano.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piano' is the musical marking for soft, abbreviated P.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspect something is to scrutinise it carefully for faults or details.

clue.text: At home, family shuns one student for notoriety

indicators.note: to shun is to keep away from, so those letters are left out

blocks.note: someone at home is in
taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one
L is for learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A household disowns one of its children who is at college, over a scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Student' is L, from the learner plates British novice drivers display; 'one' is the Roman numeral I.
explanation.definitionFit: Infamy is being well known for something bad, which is exactly what notoriety means.

clue.text: Weapon I had in river

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

blocks.note: I'd is the contraction of I had
the Trent is a major English river

explanation.surface: Someone admits to having had a weapon in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Trent flows through the English Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: A trident is a three-pronged spear, carried by Neptune and by ancient gladiators.

clue.text: Suspend setter, perhaps looking guilty

blocks.note: to hang is to suspend
a setter is a breed of dog

explanation.surface: A call to ban the crossword compiler, who seems to have something to hide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' tempts as the compiler of the puzzle; here it is the gun dog breed.
explanation.definitionFit: A hangdog expression is shamefaced and sheepish, the look of someone caught doing wrong.

clue.text: America’s corniest presenter welcomes king and Idris Elba to start with

indicators.note: to welcome someone is to take them in, so pieces go inside another
to start with points to the opening letter of each word

blocks.note: a show's presenter is its host
K is the chess abbreviation for king
the initial letters of the two names

explanation.surface: A cheesy American TV host greets royalty and a famous actor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'America's' flags that the answer is a US word; hokey is American for sentimental or corny. Idris Elba is a British actor.
explanation.definitionFit: Hokey is American slang for overly sentimental or contrived, so the superlative matches most corny.

clue.text: Country musical on the radio

indicators.note: radio is heard rather than seen, so the word is judged by its sound

blocks.note: Grease is the 1970s rock-and-roll stage show and film

explanation.surface: A country-and-western show is being broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country musical' suggests country music; the words split into definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Greece is the European nation in the south-east Mediterranean with Athens as its capital.

clue.text: Loud declaration at a wedding – pet name?

blocks.note: F is forte, the musical marking for loud
the vow spoken by bride and groom

explanation.surface: A couple shout their vows and wonder whether it counts as a nickname.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loud' is not a sound signal here but the musical abbreviation F. The question mark flags that 'pet name' means a name for a pet.
explanation.definitionFit: Fido is the stereotypical name given to a dog, so it is a name typically used for an animal companion.

clue.text: Tense row after select English strikers don’t want you to cross this

definitions.text: strikers don’t want you to cross this

blocks.note: to select is to pick
E is the abbreviation for English
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.walkthrough: 'Strikers' looks like footballers but means people on strike, and 'row' looks like a quarrel but means a line.
explanation.definitionFit: Workers on strike stand at the entrance and urge colleagues and deliveries not to go through.

clue.text: Wastes time heading away from creeps

explanation.walkthrough: 'Creeps' looks like a noun for nasty people, but it is the verb sidles.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who idles loafs about doing nothing useful, which is frittering away the hours.

the first letter of the word

clue.text: Showy statue – it soon gets destroyed
